To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neutrino telescopes IceCube and KM3NeT are able to detect signals of inert doublet model dark matter in the Sun with a significance of up to 5.6 sigma and that the neutrino telescope ANTARES is sensitive to inert doublet model annihilation in the Earth with a significance up to 4.4 sigma.
the IceCube experiment can probe the parameter space of the Inert Doublet Model (IDM) up to the TeV scale.

the neutrino flux from inert doublet annihilations in the core of the Sun can reach the level of 10-2 GeV-1 cm-2 s-1, while the neutrino fluxes from inert doublet annihilation in the Earth core and in the atmosphere can be as high as 0.1 GeV-1cm-2 s- 1 and 0.01 GeV-1 s-1 sr-1 respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for the so-called inert doublet dark model, which is one of the simplest extensions to the standard model of particle physics.
the detection of dark matter with neutrino telescope.
the study of dark matter in the Universe and its interactions with the standard model particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neutrino telescopes have a very small chance to detect the dark matter particles.
the neutrino telescopes are not able to detect the inert doublet dark-matter.
there is no evidence for the existence of dark matter in the Universe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that neutrino detectors can be used to search for the dark matter candidate in inert doublet model and the results can be used as a complementary to other indirect searches.
the neutrino telescopes have a potential to probe inert doublet dark sector up to the mass of 100 GeV, and the sensitivity can reach up to 10 TeV in some cases.

the neutrino flux from inert doublet annihilations in the Sun is too low to be detected with present-day experiments, while the Earth neutrino flux is within reach of current detectors, but the expected signal is too weak for a conclusive detection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the detection rate of neutrinos from inert doublet model dark matter annihilations at IceCube is comparable to the rate from neutrino emission from atmospheric muons.
the neutrino detection rates are very small for the parameter space that can explain the observed dark matter abundance.
the neutrino telescopes are able to probe a significant fraction of the allowed parameter space in the inert doublet dark model.
